basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A concept is a unit of meaning independent of any label, language or storage format.
Unlike a lexical entry, it does not model word forms or senses of a language.
Unlike an ontology class, it carries no formal axioms for reasoning.
Unlike a free tag, it has stable identity, definitions and governance.

may: Establish a concept identity and attach designations in several languages.
Resolve a label to candidate concepts with ambiguity shown.
Assert relations within a scheme and mappings across schemes.
mustNot: Change a concept's meaning while keeping its identifier.
Edit a published release in place.
Advance a lifecycle state without recorded authority.
Publish evidence that identifies a living person without permission.
Claim conformance to an external vocabulary standard without evidence.
requiresHuman: Approving a new or changed definition.
Deprecating a concept that others depend on.

considerations: Terms used for people and groups can stigmatise; labels should be reviewed for respectful usage.
Biased definitions propagate into systems that classify people.
Minority languages deserve equal standing in designations.
affectedParties: Users of systems built on the vocabulary

items: A concept has a persistent identifier, at least one preferred label, a definition and a scheme membership.
Often confused with a word, an ontology class, a code value and the real-world thing it denotes.
Misinterpretation when one label resolves to the wrong concept.
